angle.mindtct_authority: NBIS 5.0.0 mindtct/src/lib/mindtct/xytreps.c — XYT without -m1 is NIST internal representation: origin bottom-left, degrees 0..360, 0 pointing east, increasing counter clockwise; results.c selects NIST_INTERNAL_XYT_REP when -m1 is absent
angle.openafis_authority: lib/TripletScalar.cpp relates a minutia's angle to rotateAngle(angle, atan2(dy, dx)) over the stored coordinates, so it requires counter-clockwise from +x in the same plane as the stored y — which MINDTCT's representation already is
angle.rule: radians = degrees * pi / 180; no inversion, no rotation
angle.verification: decoding an OpenAFIS ISO template the way its own ISO parser does, including its 360-minus-angle step, and re-emitting it through this CSV path reproduces the ISO route's score exactly on twelve pairs

bounds.authority: lib/Template.h; Template::load refuses anything outside them
bounds.classification: ALGORITHMIC, not BLOCKING — a real limit of a real matcher meeting a real property of real rolled prints
bounds.why_refused: choosing which minutiae survive is a selection rule neither upstream project publishes, and the resulting score would be fpbench's rather than what MINDTCT and OpenAFIS produce between them

coordinates.csv_header: the prepared image's real width and height
coordinates.why: OpenAFIS's MinutiaPoint normalises by 256/width and 256/height itself, so any normalisation here would be applied twice

minutia_type.proved_by: scoring the same minutiae all-RidgeEnding and all-RidgeBifurcation and requiring the identical result
minutia_type.why: OpenAFIS's MinutiaPoint is built from x, y and angle only and the triplets are built from MinutiaPoint, so the type never reaches the similarity computation

quality.why: OpenAFIS has nowhere to put it, and filtering on it would be a minutiae-selection rule fpbench invented
